engine_gap.behavior: A single stage's procedure must ask the user several separate, sequentially dependent questions (project name, then a variable number of per-repository rounds, then a variable number of per-group rounds, then default instructions, identity, and graphify path), stopping and waiting for each answer before formulating the next question, where the total number of question rounds is not known until the user answers earlier ones.
engine_gap.source_evidence: sergeant-setup/SKILL.md lines 169-184 ('Ask these questions in order; stop and wait for each answer before proceeding', followed by 'for each repository' and 'for each named group' sub-loops); corroborated by the same 'ask, wait for the user's answer' pattern at lines 109-114 (clone destination) and the explicit backup/diff/confirm sequence at Phase 5 (lines 204-216).
lower_rungs_attempted: One actor stage per phase, with the whole multi-question interview embedded in one CONTEXT.md turn.
One coarse Work needs_input round-trip per phase, collecting all of a phase's answers together.
One stage per individual question, splitting Phase 4 into a fixed number of stages.
engine_gap.why_each_fails: One actor stage per phase fails because the measured Claude adapter (GAUNTLET D2, confirmed at M4) drives bounded headless `claude -p --output-format stream-json` turns with no TTY/pane; a turn either completes or it does not, so nothing inside one turn can suspend after question 1, wait for an out-of-band answer, and then resume the same reasoning context to ask question 2. A coarse per-phase needs_input round-trip changes the skill's own specified semantics: it requires 'stop and wait for each answer before proceeding' one question at a time so that an early answer (e.g. zero repositories) can end the interview before later questions are even asked; collecting all answers in one round-trip cannot express that early-stop behavior. One stage per individual question is expressible today for the fixed-count parts (project name, defaults, identity, graphify path) but not for the per-repository and per-group loops, whose round count depends on the user's own prior answers -- the current engine requires a workflow's stage list to be a statically pinned, resolved-before-Work-starts sequence (proposal §3.3, 'journal the resolved WorkflowDefinition before execution'), which cannot express a variable number of stages decided at runtime.
engine_gap.minimum_runtime_capability_required: Either (a) a stage class that can emit a structured question, suspend the stage's attempt without ending its trajectory, and resume the same actor context after an API-delivered answer -- an intra-stage needs_input loop distinct from today's whole-Work needs_input -- or (b) a stage-list mechanism that can expand a bounded, data-driven set of question rounds at runtime while remaining journaled and replayable across a restart.
engine_gap.observable_acceptance_test: A workflow stage can ask N sequential, dependent questions where N is determined by earlier answers (e.g., one question per repository the user names), journaling each answer against the same stage attempt and resuming the same actor identity/context after each answer without restarting the stage or losing prior answers, verified across a daemon restart mid-interview.

engine_gap.behavior: A single logical cross-repository task ('fleet') must durably group N independent per-repository dispatches -- each an isolated git worktree plus its own agent execution -- under one identity, track each member's individual state, honor declared dependency edges between members (e.g. smith-infra>smith), and support fleet-scoped monitoring, response delivery, and cleanup as one durable object, while each member also remains individually retryable/recoverable.
engine_gap.source_evidence: dispatch/SKILL.md line 84 ('Creates fleet state at ~/.local/share/sergeant/fleet/<task-id>/'); dispatch/SKILL.md lines 88-92 (sgt-watch aggregating per-repo .sergeant-status/.sergeant-message/.sergeant-result into one live fleet table); dispatch/SKILL.md lines 149-157 (--deps 'a>b,a>c' dependency notation, with 'the workers themselves are responsible for honoring this' -- i.e. no runtime enforcement today either); dispatch/SKILL.md lines 117-119 (sgt-cleanup <task-id> removing worktrees and fleet state for the whole task at once); cross-repo-work/SKILL.md lines 42-43 (the same prerequisite>dependent notation, produced by planning and consumed by dispatch).
lower_rungs_attempted: Represent the whole cross-repo task as one Work, with per-repo dispatches as ordinary sequential stages of that one Work.
Represent each repository's dispatch as its own independent top-level Work, coordinated only by convention (e.g. a shared task-id string embedded in each Work's metadata).
Represent fan-out and dependency edges purely as authored workflow content: a stage's CONTEXT.md instructs the actor to submit N separate `sgt run` invocations and poll them.
engine_gap.why_each_fails: One Work with per-repo dispatches as stages fails because today's Work owns exactly one Git surface (proposal §3.6, runtime/surface.rs) and one backend/session for the whole run (§3.5); a stage cannot fan out into N independently-progressing, independently-recoverable native harness sessions each in its own worktree, and a single stage's completion is one BackendSignal, not N concurrent ones. N independent top-level Works coordinated only by a shared string fails because the engine itself has no fleet/parent identity to query: dependency edges (smith-infra>smith) cannot be enforced or even observed by the engine, only inferred by an external actor re-reading each Work's state one at a time, and a crash mid-fan-out leaves no journaled record of which Works belong to which fleet or what the intended dependency graph was -- exactly the ambiguity CLAUDE.md's 'ambiguity fails closed' invariant says must not be silently guessed past. Authored-content fan-out (actor-issued `sgt run` calls) is explicitly rejected by §7.7/§10.3: it hides the parent/child relationship from the parent workflow, and dispatch's own contract already requires exactly the visibility that loses (sgt-watch's live per-repo status table, and sgt-respond addressed by both task-id and repo).
engine_gap.minimum_runtime_capability_required: A durable fleet/parent-task identity that groups a fixed or dynamically-declared set of member Works, records declared dependency edges between members, exposes fleet-scoped read views (aggregate status, per-member state) through the API, and supports fleet-scoped operations (respond to one member, cancel/clean up the whole fleet) whose effects are journaled against both the member Work and the fleet identity.
engine_gap.observable_acceptance_test: Submitting one cross-repo task creates one fleet record referencing N member Works with declared dependency edges; the API can list all N members and their states under the fleet id; a dependent member is held (not merely advised) until its declared prerequisite member reaches a terminal successful state, purely from journaled evidence; and canceling or cleaning up the fleet id transitions/removes exactly its N members, verified after a daemon restart mid-fleet.

## Treehouse worktrees

Sergeant prefers [treehouse](https://github.com/kunchenguid/treehouse) for worktree management. Treehouse maintains a pool of pre-warmed worktrees per repo — leasing one is faster than `git worktree add` and cleanup is pooled.

**How dispatch uses treehouse:**
- If `treehouse.toml` exists in a repo → `treehouse get --lease --lease-holder "sgt-<task-id>-<repo>"`

- Cleanup via `treehouse return <path>`

When a route fails after parsing, the router retains a sanitized findings artifact under `.sergeant-review-artifacts/<axis>-<source>/` and names the exact `sgt-review-findings <project> <repo> --retry <path> --worktree <path>` command; retry from that artifact rather than re-running the reviewer, and never delete a retained artifact that has not been retried

trigger: a review finding fails to route
outcome: evidence is preserved and addressable rather than silently dropped or expensively re-derived
notes: Strong parallel to CLAUDE.md's evidence-preservation ethos (the journal is the only truth; nothing is silently re-derived when durable evidence already exists).
rationale: A recovery-path detail for the review-routing procedure (BU-P5-082); it has no completion evidence and only matters when routing already failed, so it stays as context rather than its own stage.

statement: A stored finding-card revision the router cannot prove it authored is preserved below a superseded-revision separator and the card gains a needs-reconciliation label; only the worker owning the finding may merge the two accounts and remove that label -- the router itself never clears it.

source.quote: 14. A stored card revision the router cannot prove it authored is kept below a `--- Superseded revision (preserved) ---` separator and the card gains the `needs-reconciliation` label. The worker owning the finding merges the two accounts and removes that label; the router never clears it, so a card still carrying it has an open reconciliation obligation

trigger: the router would otherwise overwrite a card revision it did not create
outcome: concurrent writers to the same card never silently clobber each other; reconciliation is an explicit, owned obligation
notes: A genuinely reusable append-then-flag-for-reconciliation concurrency-safety pattern, resembling CLAUDE.md's adjacent-append crash-window class (LESSONS L6).
rationale: A concurrency-safety rule for the same review-card writes BU-P5-083 concerns; no independent checkpoint, so kept as context (already flagged as a shared-context candidate in its own alternatives_considered).
alternatives_considered: shared-context (noted, not claimed here): this reconciliation-label pattern could generalize beyond findings cards to any concurrently-writable durable record; flagged for helper-map/shared-context-map consideration rather than asserted as already-generalized in the corpus.

statement: Findings sharing the same originating run, head, owning module, and root cause share one serialized remediation worker/branch; before merging that group, native tests and independent re-reviews verifying mutation-before-validation, partial-publication/rollback, and identity/provenance are rerun; after two remediation cycles, fix dispatch stops and an architectural/root-cause review plus a human decision is required.

source.quote: 15. Keep one TD record per no-mistakes finding. Findings with the same originating run, head, owning module, and root cause share one serialized remediation worker/branch. Remediation never runs no-mistakes; before merging the group, rerun native tests and independent rereviews that verify mutation before validation, partial publication or rollback, and identity/provenance, then resume the retained run. After two remediation cycles, stop fix dispatch and require architectural/root-cause review p

trigger: multiple findings share a root cause
outcome: remediation is deduplicated, re-verified before merge, and escalates to a human after bounded retries rather than looping indefinitely
rationale: Describes how remediation work stemming from findings is grouped and bounded; it has no single completion evidence of its own (it governs a whole sub-loop, not one checkpoint), and unlike the routing/label rules above it is not deterministic enough to be a helper, so it stays as stage-context.

statement: A worker writes its terminal result record and sets its status to done only after every completion gate has passed; a failed status with an exact reason is reserved specifically for an unrecoverable terminal failure.

source.quote: 19. Write `.sergeant-result` and set `.sergeant-status=done` only after every gate passes. `failed: <exact reason>` is reserved for an unrecoverable terminal failure

trigger: a worker reaches a terminal outcome
outcome: the terminal status distinguishes verified success from unrecoverable failure, and neither is asserted prematurely
notes: The file-based status mechanism is obsolete; the durable contract it encodes -- an explicit terminal-state distinction requiring all gates before success, mirroring WorkState's completed/failed distinction and the 'completed and canceled Work are absorbing' invariant -- is not. Old-Sergeant mechanism: the .sergeant-result file.
rationale: The worker's terminal-status discipline, mirroring WorkState's completed/failed distinction; it is the last item of the worker's ordered contract rather than a separate observable checkpoint of dispatch itself, so it is context, not a new stage.

statement: If a canonical skill referenced by the routing table cannot be loaded, the generated brief's own embedded rules for that phase remain mandatory regardless.

source.quote: If a canonical skill cannot be loaded, the generated brief's embedded rules remain mandatory for that phase.

trigger: a canonical skill named by the routing table is unavailable
outcome: the phase's requirements still apply even without the specialized skill loaded
rationale: A degradation/fallback policy for the workflow-composition pattern discussed in the attached engine-gap: today, the fallback is duplicated prose in the generated brief rather than an engine-owned default.

statement: Dispatching from a free-form brief creates exactly one td task per target repository before spawning any worker; if td is unavailable, task creation fails, generated metadata cannot be injected, or any selected repo fails to get a task, the whole dispatch aborts before spawning any worker and rolls back the generated tasks.

source.quote:
## td task creation

When you dispatch from a freeform brief, `sgt-dispatch` creates exactly one td task in each target repo before spawning any worker. If td is unavailable, task creation fails, generated task metadata cannot be injected, or any selected repo does not get a generated task, dispatch aborts before spawning and rolls back the generated cards. `--td` dispatch keeps using the existing task instead of generating replacements.

trigger: a free-form dispatch is being launched
outcome: task creation for a multi-repo dispatch is all-or-nothing, never partially committed before any agent starts
notes: An atomicity/rollback invariant on the pre-flight side of dispatch -- resembles the adjacent-append crash-window concern class (commit fully or roll back before any irreversible side effect).
rationale: A rollback/atomicity guarantee on the 20-dispatch stage's own task-creation step; it has no completion evidence distinct from BU-P5-070's later reconcile gates or from dispatch succeeding at all, so it is context on 20-dispatch rather than its own checkpoint.

statement: Recovering a stuck, stale, or orphaned dispatched worker is done only through the response-delivery command or an equivalent explicit action; a worker is never marked done manually, and a retry writes both the result and the done status only after every completion gate passes.

source.quote:
## Troubleshooting

| Symptom | Fix |
|---|---|
| Worker stuck, no status update | `tmux attach -t sgt-<task-id>` and check the window |
| Worktree creation fails | Check if branch already exists; use `--branch` with a unique name |
| Fleet state is stale | Run `bin/sgt-watch --sync <task-id>` to force a one-shot sync |
| Need to recover a waiting or orphaned worker | Use `bin/sgt-respond <task-id> <repo> "<response>"`; do not mark it done manually |
| Need to retry a failed repo | Fix the under

trigger: a worker appears stuck, stale, or orphaned
outcome: recovery never fabricates a successful terminal state; it either delivers an explicit response or nothing changes
notes: Corroborates the 'ambiguity fails closed'/no-guessing invariant already present in sergeant-rs (CLAUDE.md §4.3): old Sergeant's own troubleshooting guidance already refuses to let an operator hand-mark uncertain state as done. Old-Sergeant mechanism: sgt-respond.
rationale: A safety constraint on how a stuck worker may be recovered; it applies across the whole dispatch workflow's monitor/recover path rather than to one stage, and it produces no completion evidence of its own (recovery either succeeds via BU-P5-067's normal channel or nothing changes), so it is workflow-scoped context, not a new stage.

statement: load-project resolves Sergeant project ownership, configuration, and paths before any work begins.
